subject: Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))

messages.author: 716b3fb4344acd58
messages.subject: Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
parts:
Dear group,

I´m new to GGIR and am trying to get advanced sleeplog to work. I´ve been searching this forum for this error but could not find similar problem. We have tried on two computers but on both get this error message: 

Part 4 Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed In addition: Warning message: In g.loadlog(params_sleep[["loglocation"]], coln1 = params_sleep[["coln1"]], : NAs introduced by coercion
The code runs with basic sleeplog as well as no sleeplog configured, but gets into trouble with the advaned log.
I´ve tried to make the sleeplog as the example in the documentation and saved it as csv-file. 
Here is part of my script: 

--Sleep analysis, SIB and SPT--
  loglocation = c("C:/Users/Mikael/Documents/!Motoriklab Projekt/ActiGraph - Ferdinands projekt/R - GGIR/Input/KR Grupp1 Pre/Sleeplog_Pre01.csv"),
  colid = 1,
  coln1 = 2,
  sleeplogsep = ";",
  nnights = 7,
  sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed",
  ignorenonwear = TRUE,
  HASIB.algo = "vanHees2015",
  HASPT.algo = "HDCZA",  

I would very much apprechiate idéas on what to try. I can also share the script and the log if it would help, I could not attach any files to this message.

Kind regards
Mikael

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
parts:
Dear Mikael,

The error indicates that something goes wrong with reading or processing the sleeplog file. Common problems are that ID's do not match or the separator is not valid.

Did you check that ID is correctly extract from the accelerometer file? This can be checked by inspecting the part2_summary.csv report. The ID column in that file should be identical to the ID column in the sleeplog file.

You can check the separator in Notepad for example.

After you change the sleeplog to advanced did you re-run GGIR part 3 and 4?
I can also share the script and the log if it would help, I could not attach any files to this message.

Yes, that could help, even if it is just the relevant lines.

Thanks,
Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error when using advanced sleeplog (Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2))
parts:
Hi Mikael,

This is bug in GGIR: There are no sustained inactivity bouts in the first night and GGIR cannot handle this. It is very unusual to not have any of them as it would mean that the person has not rested or slept for the first 24 hours or the device was in ActiGraph idle sleep mode for the first 24 hours, which would explain that I had not seen this before.

I have prepared a fix, which you can try out via installing GGIR as follows:

install.package("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue812_absence_sib_firstday")
library(GGIR)

A second problem is that you did not specify argument idloc when you processed the file with GGIR part 1, by which GGIR did not attempt to extract the ID from the accelerometer file name and as a result will struggle to match this with the ID as stored in the sleeplog.

Kind regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks for looking into this. I tried to install the modified package as suggested with the fix, but I receive the same error message when running the script with either of my 2 versions of the sleeplog.
I did specify idloc=2 in the script from the beginning, and from what I could see it matched the ID with the right part from the filename.

Yes the problem with this dataset is that the recording started one day too early so they contain at least 24 h with Actigraph idle sleep. I have since starting to learn GGIR understood that keeping this on is not a good idéa. We have other datasets that have mixed non-wear-time, some in the beginning of the file for a whole day, others in the middle or the end. Some subjects took the accelerometer off before sleeping. The study protocol was for 7 consecutive days.

/Mikael

Den mån 26 juni 2023 kl 16:21 skrev Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com>:
Hi Mikael,

This is bug in GGIR: There are no sustained inactivity bouts in the first night and GGIR cannot handle this. It is very unusual to not have any of them as it would mean that the person has not rested or slept for the first 24 hours or the device was in ActiGraph idle sleep mode for the first 24 hours, which would explain that I had not seen this before.

I have prepared a fix, which you can try out via installing GGIR as follows:

install.package("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue812_absence_sib_firstday")
library(GGIR)

A second problem is that you did not specify argument idloc when you processed the file with GGIR part 1, by which GGIR did not attempt to extract the ID from the accelerometer file name and as a result will struggle to match this with the ID as stored in the sleeplog.

Kind regards,

Vincent
